rulings.Case Title: KRISSIA VANESSA GONZALEZ VS. FERRY GUNAMWAN
rulings.Calendar Matter: Notice Of Motion To Correct Clerical Error In Clerks Judgment
rulings.Rulings: Matter on calendar for Friday, July 17, 2026, Line 1, CALIFORNIA LABOR COMMISSIONER'S OFFICE (NON-PARTY) Motion To Correct Clerical Error In Clerks Judgment. The unopposed motion to correct a clerical error in the court's judgment, to wit the misspelling of defendant Ferry Gunawan's name (erroneously spelled in the judgment as "Ferry Gunamwan"), is granted. The amended judgment shall be corrected nunc pro tunc to the date of entry of October 30, 2024. Moving party California Labor Commissioner's Office shall submit a proposed amended judgment. For the 9:00 a.m. calendar, all attorneys and parties may appear in Department 301 remotely or in person. Remote hearings will be conducted by videoconference using Zoom. (Dept. 301 Zoom ID 161 502 4290; Passcode 700956.) To appear remotely at the hearing, go to the court's website at sfsuperiorcourt.org under "Online Services," navigate to "Tentative Rulings," and click on the appropriate link, or dial the corresponding phone number. Any party who contests a tentative ruling must send an email to contestdept301tr@sftc.org with a copy to all other parties by 4pm stating, without argument, the portion(s) of the tentative ruling that the party contests. The subject line of the email shall include the line number, case name and case number. The text of the email shall include the name and contact information, including email address, of the attorney or party who will appear at the hearing. The court no longer provides a court reporter in the Law & Motion or Discovery Department. Parties may retain their own reporter, who may appear in the courtroom or remotely. A retained reporter must be a California certified court reporter (CSR), for only a CSR's transcript may be used in California courts. If a CSR is being retained, include in your email all of the following: their name, CSR and telephone numbers, and their individual work email address. =(301/CVA).

rulings.Rulings: Matter on calendar for Friday, July 17, 2026, Line 8, PLAINTIFF EMA BELL's Motion To Approve Proposition 65 Settlement And Consent Judgment. The court grants the unopposed motion to approve the Proposition 65 settlement and consent judgment. The court finds that the settlement is in compliance with Proposition 65 (Health & Safety Code, sections 25249.5 to 25249.14); the award of attorney's fees pursuant to the settlement is reasonable under California law on the evidence before the court; and that, considering the factors set out in Health & Safety Code, section 25249.7, subdivision (b)(2), and the facts asserted in the moving papers, the penalty amount is reasonable.
